articles.title: ‘Mom encouraged me to get breast implants’: Disney child star Christy Carlson Romano on fame, family and freedom
articles.summary: She started acting at six and by 16 was starring in Even Stevens with Shia LaBeouf. Then her career fell apart. Here, she explains how she survived growing up in the spotlight. In a class at college, Christy Carlson Romano was encouraged to think about her “community”.
body: The title of her memoir, Once Upon a Trainwreck, gives you a flavour of where Carlson Romano, 42, is coming from, but what’s most striking isn’t that she goes off the rails (she doesn’t, hugely, compared to other former child stars), but how sensible and mature she is as a child. It’s alarming. When fans recognise her now – she was in the popular Disney series Even Stevens which started in 2000 – they tell her she was a huge part of their childhoods. She had been acting the part of a normal suburban girl, the perfectionist Ren Stevens, while having no idea what that was like. She was already a mini adult.

Now Carlson Romano has a social media career, which has given her a detachment from the entertainment industry. “I’m outspoken at this point, but for a lot of people they can’t do that,” she says. “What hurts is when I see other child actors suffering, because I know that means they haven’t found their way through the pain.” We speak, over Zoom, not long after Hayden Panettiere, the “Nashville” actor and singer who had started as a child and had talked about her experience of early fame, addiction and mental illness, had been found dead.

articles.title: ‘Too many stories exist only to make you think you’re on the right side’: Cristian Mungiu on Fjord, the Cannes winner that divided Europe
articles.summary: The Romanian auteur’s new film could have been the kind of homogenous ‘Europudding’ he’s railed against for years. Instead, it’s a culture-clash skewering of conservative and liberal values worthy of its Palme d’Or. ‘Pffff!” Cristian Mungiu lets out an exasperated sigh.
body: In 2013, Mungiu was part of a delegation of European auteurs who travelled to Brussels to meet the then president of the European Commission, José Manuel Barroso. At the time, the EU and US were in talks to slash barriers to trade between the two economic blocs, and the film-makers were lobbying the Commission to spare their industry from the deal.

If countries weren’t allowed to subsidise their own productions, one argument went, European cinema would become a stolid mush of homogenised co-productions – “Europudding”, as people called it at the time. To those ends, they would no longer be able to create national dramas like Mungiu’s own 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, a riveting abortion thriller set in cold war-era Bucharest that had won the Palme d’Or at Cannes in 2007.

articles.title: Rocky review – 50 years on Stallone’s boxer remains a gritty contender
articles.summary: The actor’s triumphant breakthrough has clear ancestors in grimy tales of working-class struggle, but finds a fresh, rousing idealism. Peter Farrelly’s new film I Play Rocky is about the underdog-with-heart story of how a great boxing movie got made against the odds with its plucky young untried…
body: Rocky thoughtfully tells Adrian how tough boxing is, how loaded it is against fighters like him, and how it is almost designed to turn boxers into wrecks. When a movie audience hears that Rocky has been promised $150,000 as his share of the purse, they must wince with anticipation at the betrayal that is surely coming. He’s going to get cheated of that fortune … isn’t he? Similarly, when the loathsome Gazzo gives Rocky $500 for training expenses, we wince again. Rocky is now in debt to this gangster. Gazzo is going to demand some sort of quid quo pro. Will Rocky be asked to take a dive?

The answer in both cases, by a kind of miracle, is no. (Or at least we can assume that the answer to the first is no, and definitely no to the second.) Rocky is a film that appears to remember the melancholy destiny of Brando in On the Waterfront and also the ugly racial contest in something like The Great White Hope, which starred James Earl Jones as the Jim Crow-era black boxer Jack Johnson. But it turns despair on its head.

articles.title: Marilyn Monroe Retrospective at Torino to Portray Her as a ‘Female Marlon Brando’: ‘She Was So Profound’
articles.summary: The dust had barely settled on last year’s Torino Film Festival when artistic director Giulio Base began plotting his next move. 2026 would mark the centenary of Marilyn Monroe’s birth, and Base was determined not to be beaten to it.
body: The gambit paid off twice over. Announced just before the 2025 festival closed, the showcase staked Torino’s claim and gave Base’s team a focal point around which to build the new program.

This year’s 24-film lineup stretches well beyond Monroe’s own filmography. Classics like “The Seven Year Itch,” “How to Marry a Millionaire” and “Some Like It Hot” sit alongside revisionist takes such as Andrew Dominik’s “Blonde” and Pier Paolo Pasolini and Giovanni Guareschi’s documentary “La Rabbia” because the star’s relatively brief career simply didn’t offer enough leading roles to fill the schedule.

“Screening a movie where she has only a scene that isn’t even relevant would be a pity,” Base says. “So we decided to understand her complete legend, including the movies that celebrate her, or research her life, her problems, her traumas, her faults and her dreams.”

articles.title: Russell Brand’s Marriage to Katy Perry Blocked From Being Mentioned by Prosecution in Rape Trial
articles.summary: Russell Brand’s marriage to Katy Perry was reportedly blocked from being mentioned in the prosecution’s opening arguments in his London rape and sexual assault trial following objections from the comedian’s legal team.
body: According to details of pre-trial proceedings made public after his conviction, prosecutors had planned to reference Brand’s relationship with Perry, whom he married in 2010. However, his defense successfully challenged the inclusion of the singer in the prosecution’s opening statement, arguing against introducing details of his personal life that were unrelated to the allegations.

“The prosecution recognise that matters post 2009 involving his relationship with Katy Perry may be sensitive, as may his previous faiths, and we are content to remove these from the opening,” lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC said in pre-trial submissions, according to a report from The Telegraph.

Perry was also reportedly not asked to provide a witness statement during the police investigation. Although her name was absent from the prosecution’s opening remarks, Brand himself referenced their marriage while testifying, describing the period as one in which he achieved “staggering fame.”
The former couple began dating in 2009. They married in a Hindu ceremony in Rajasthan, India, the following year, before separating in December 2011. Their divorce was finalized in 2012.

articles.summary: A producer who is alleged to have laughed while Russell Brand put his head on a woman’s groin has stepped back from his role as head of comedy at the London production company behind Michaela Coel’s sexual assault drama “I May Destroy You.” Jack Bayles, head of comedy at Various Artists Limited…
body: According to The Times, the court heard that Bayles and another member of Brand’s entourage, Gareth Roy, said the comedian would only continue working if the complainant gave him a massage. She complained to her bosses at Channel 4 the next day.
The woman’s workplace manager, who gave evidence during the trial, said the victim had complained to her how she was told several times to “just do it” by Bayles and Roy.

During the incident Brand also put his head in the woman’s groin area. In a statement to the court, the manager said she was told the men “were both there the whole time and watched and laughed while Mr Brand sexually assaulted her right in front of them,” according to The Times.
Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting the Channel 4 employee on Thursday along with two other counts of sexual assault and one count of rape.

articles.title: Taiwan Should Bet on Horror to Crack Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s Biggest Film Market, Study Finds
articles.summary: Horror stands out as a natural meeting ground for Taiwanese and Indonesian producers, according to a K7 Media study of the Indonesian film and TV market presented by Trang Nguyen at Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei. The stakes are considerable.
body: Local films rule the multiplexes. Indonesian titles made up 201, or 43%, of 2025 releases but took 64% of admissions, with 82.6 million tickets sold, per Cinepoint data via the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM). That is more than double the 36.9 million admissions for the 100 U.S. releases. Other Asian imports barely registered: 27 Japanese films drew 3.3 million admissions, while 61 Korean and 16 Chinese titles each pulled in 2 million.

Three local titles sit in the 10 million-plus club: Imajinari’s 2025 comedy “Agak Laen: Menyala Pantiku!,” Visinema’s 2025 animated fantasy adventure “Jumbo” and MD Pictures’ 2022 horror “KKN di Desa Penari.”

Horror is the genre Indonesia produces most for cinemas. Five of the 10 most-attended Indonesian films since 2011 are horror pictures, and recent hits have mixed scares with comedy or drama. Many of the country’s horror films draw on existing IP. Foreign horror can break out too. Korean hit “Exhuma” drove up local theatrical interest in Korean films after its 2024 run. The presentation singled out “The Rope Curse 4” as a recent Taiwan-Indonesia collaboration.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo's Christmas song sounds familiar... on purpose
articles.summary: The pop star sought permission from cult 80s band The Waitresses before releasing her festive single.
body: Pop star Olivia Rodrigo unwrapped her first-ever Christmas song on Thursday night, alongside a festive music video starring Sex and the City star Cynthia Nixon.
The track, called Take Me Home (4 Christmas), finds the pop star asking her boyfriend to "show some serious commitment" by bringing her to his parents' house for the Christmas break.
As soon as it was released, fans noticed similarities to The Waitresses' 1981 festive hit Christmas Wrapping... And it turns out that was by design rather than mistake.
Chris Butler, who wrote The Waitresses' song, posted a message on Facebook, external, saying Rodrigo had contacted him to seek permission for the song; and praising her "phenomenal" writing.

articles.title: Met Police boss 'wouldn't be surprised' if more allegations made about Brand
articles.summary: Sir Mark Rowley also said what he heard reported from Brand's trial came close to "victim blaming".
body: The head of the Metropolitan Police has said he "wouldn't be surprised" if more people came forward to make allegations about Russell Brand.
Sir Mark Rowley also said that what he heard reported from Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court came very close to "victim blaming".
On Thursday, the entertainer and comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
He was acquitted of two other rape charges and one allegation of attempted indecent assault. The 51-year-old will be sentenced on Monday.

articles.title: “Saviors of Cinema” and “Money Machine”: Tallinn Puts Spotlight on Kids, Youth Films and Social Media Bans
articles.summary: Kärt Väinola, the head of the Just Film Industry Days, taking place during the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival, also previews how AI and labels will be debated during its fourth edition.
body: Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) kicks off its 30th anniversary edition on Friday. In addition to latest art house discoveries, movies for younger audiences will also take the spotlight at the event – as has become tradition.

PÖFF launched its popular Just Film Festival for youth and children’s movies in 2001. Since 2023, it has also organized the Just Film Industry Days to provide networking, education and pitching opportunities for people working in or looking at the space.

Kärt Väinola is the head of Just Film Industry Days, along with serving as Baltic Event Co-Production and International Works in Progress co-manager, Just Film Works in Progress manager and panels & talks coordinator.

She talked to THR about why Tallinn has been proudly putting the spotlight on kids and youth content, how it fits into broader industry trends and why social media bans, whether launched and considered, will be among the hot topics of discussion this year.

articles.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK crowns winner as BBC axes the series
articles.summary: The UK spin off of the global hit show is being shelved after eight series on the BBC.
body: Warning: This article includes spoilers for the finale of RuPaul's Drag Race UK.
After 10 weeks of toe-to-toe lip-syncs, fierce runways and shady remarks, the time has come for one queen to be named the UK's next Drag Race superstar.
For the final time on the BBC, 12 contestants were whittled down to just one after the broadcaster announced it was axing RuPaul's Drag Race UK due to budget cuts.
The London queen snatched the title from Mocha, Naya Thorn and Alik who also made it to the final episode.
